blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A nightly job calls `pool.submit(() -> archive(day))` for each day of the month and moves on without keeping the returned futures. For one day, archive() throws a NullPointerException on a malformed record. Nothing else in the job or the pool has been customised. What does the job's output show for that day?

options.text: Nothing, since the pool keeps the exception for a later call to get() on that task's future
options.says: a task given to submit has its exception stored in its Future, and only a call to get() reports it

options.text: Nothing, since the pool discards an unchecked exception once the task's run() has ended
options.says: the exception is not discarded: the pool stores it in the Future, where get() would report it

options.text: A stack trace from the pool thread, since the thread's handler prints what escapes the task's run()
options.says: that is what happens with execute(); submit() catches the exception and stores it in the Future, so nothing is printed

options.text: A stack trace from the pool thread, since the pool logs the task's failure before it marks it done
options.says: the pool reports nothing; the failure reaches only a caller of get()

origin.section: A Callable's Result and Its Exception Both Come Back Through get()

questions.stem: A one-thread pool has been running an export task for a minute; the export needs nine more minutes and never checks whether it was interrupted. Another export waits in the pool's queue. An admin's request calls `cancel(false)` on the running export's future. What does that call return, and when does the queued export start?

options.text: It returns false, and the queued export starts in about nine minutes, since cancel(false) leaves a task that has already started alone
options.says: cancel(false) on a running task returns true and cancels the Future; it just doesn't stop the thread

options.text: It returns true, and the queued export starts in about nine minutes, since cancel(false) marks the future cancelled and leaves its thread alone
options.says: the Future is cancelled (get() throws CancellationException), but the thread runs the export to the end before it takes the queued one

options.text: It returns true, and the queued export starts at once, since cancel(false) marks the future cancelled and frees its thread
options.says: cancel(false) gives up the result but doesn't touch the thread, which runs the export to the end before it takes the queued one

options.text: It returns false, and the queued export starts at once, since cancel(false) leaves the task alone but the pool stops waiting for it
options.says: cancel(false) returns true here, and the pool's only thread stays with the running export until it ends

origin.section: A Timed get() Ends the Wait, Not the Task

questions.stem: A loop reads the five futures returned by `invokeAll(checks, 2, SECONDS)` in order and prints each result, with a `catch (ExecutionException e)` around each get(). The first two checks finish in time, the third is still running at the deadline, and the last two finish in time. What does the loop print?

options.text: Two results, and then an exception the catch doesn't cover ends the loop, since the late check's future was cancelled
options.says: the timed invokeAll cancelled the third task; get() on a cancelled future throws the unchecked CancellationException

options.text: Two results, and then the loop waits on the third future, since the deadline ended only invokeAll's own wait for the checks
options.says: at the deadline the timed invokeAll cancels the tasks still running, and every future it returns is done

options.text: Four results and nothing for the third, since invokeAll returns only the futures of the checks that finished in time
options.says: invokeAll returns a future for every task, in the tasks' order; a late one is there, cancelled

options.text: Four results and one failure from the catch, since a check cut off by the deadline fails like any other check
options.says: a late task is cancelled, not failed: its get() throws CancellationException, not ExecutionException

origin.section: invokeAll's Deadline Cancels the Stragglers, and Their get() Throws an Unchecked CancellationException

questions.stem: A downloader gives three mirrors to `invokeAny`. Mirror A throws an IOException after 15 ms, mirror B returns the file after 60 ms, and mirror C would return it after 400 ms. What does the call do?

options.text: It throws ExecutionException after 15 ms and cancels B and C, since the call ends with the first mirror to complete
options.says: invokeAny skips a failure while another task can still succeed

options.text: It returns B's file after 60 ms and cancels C, since the call ends with the first mirror to succeed
options.says: invokeAny returns the first successful result and cancels the tasks still running

options.text: It returns B's file after 60 ms and leaves C running, since the call stops waiting but stops no mirror
options.says: invokeAny cancels the tasks still running once it has a result; in the page's run, replica 3 was interrupted at that moment

options.text: It throws ExecutionException after 15 ms and leaves B and C running, since the call stops waiting but stops no mirror
options.says: invokeAny doesn't end on a failure while another task can still succeed, and it cancels the rest once one succeeds

origin.section: invokeAny Returns the First Success, Not the First to Finish

concepts: cancel(false) on a running task returns true and cancels the Future, so get() throws CancellationException, but the thread runs the task to the end.
invokeAny returns the first successful result, skipping failures, cancels the tasks still running, and throws ExecutionException only when every task fails.
A task given to submit reports its failure only to a caller of get(); a future nobody reads fails silently, and isDone() is true for it.
